editorial.description_en: The darkest soil there is, at the point where warmth is the only thing distinguishing it from a charcoal.
editorial.description_ja: いちばん黒い土のような、深くあたたかい色。
editorial.contemporaryNote_en: The warm counterpart to 底墨. The two are close in lightness and read as different colours only against something neutral, which is the comparison the Compare surface exists to make.

provenance.derivation: Editorial construction, not a measurement. Specified in OKLCh as L 0.206, C 0.030, h 58.0° and converted to canonical D65 XYZ by @irodora/color-spaces 0.1.0 (oklchToXyz), rounded to six decimal places. Re-derivable from this sentence alone.
provenance.editorialNotes: Name coined by Irodora: 黒 (kuro, black) + 土 (tsuchi, earth). It is not asserted to be a traditional Japanese colour name, and the hyphenated romaji marks it as a constructed compound (ADR-0065). "Black Earth" is an editorial decision about what communicates in English, not a literal translation of 黒土. Relations asserted from measured proximity under the current engine, not from a source: related is the three nearest in CIELAB — ame-doro at ΔE00 5.2, doro-soko at ΔE00 10.2, soko-zumi at ΔE00 10.2. complementary is empty because at chroma 0.030 the hue is not a reliable enough statement to oppose. historicalVariants is empty: this entry makes no historical claim to vary from.
